mlb.blurb: LOS ANGELES -- Returning home to Chavez Ravine provided the Dodgers with the exact reset they needed on Monday night.
mlb.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Returning home to Chavez Ravine provided the Dodgers with the exact reset they needed on Monday night.

With the Dodgers working through a demanding stretch and searching for a spark to respond after dropping three consecutive series, the stage was set for Max Muncy on his own bobblehead giveaway night -- before Freddie Freeman delivered the decisive blow to secure a 6-5 victory over the Royals.

After Tarik Skubal fell behind early in his Dodgers home debut, Los Angeles battled through six tight innings before finding the dramatic swing it had been seeking in the bottom of the sixth. With two on and two out, manager Dave Roberts matched urgency with action, calling on pinch-hitter Kyle Tucker to bat for Teoscar Hernández against right-hander John Schreiber. Tucker drew a walk to load the bases, setting the stage for Muncy to line a bases-clearing three-run double to right field. The clutch hit brought home Tommy Edman, Miguel Rojas and Tucker, electrifying the Dodger Stadium crowd and surging the Dodgers to a 5-3 lead.

“If I talk about urgency from our guys, then I've got to manage accordingly,” Roberts said of the high-leverage move to use Tucker. “It's about winning the baseball game. Tuck gave us an opportunity by getting on base and giving Max an opportunity, and we won a ballgame.” “Just wanted something up in the zone, try not to do too much,” Muncy told SportsNet LA regarding his double. “He actually made a really good pitch, but I was able to just dunk it over the first baseman’s head, and props to the runners for going hard all the way around.” For Muncy, the game was a testament to the team’s reset mindset in the wake of their recent slump. “It doesn't matter what happened yesterday, the last week, the last month,” Muncy added. “You show up every day with an opportunity to do something great. You're 0-for-0 every single day. There's an opportunity in front of you, and that's what we have to focus on.” However, after Kansas City answered with a game-tying two-run home run from Kyle Isbel in the top of the seventh, the Dodgers needed another response in the bottom half. Shohei Ohtani sparked the rally by lining a single to center and swiping second base. Freeman then stepped to the plate and delivered the go-ahead RBI single off Alex Lange, driving in Ohtani to break the 5-5 tie and put Los Angeles back on top for good. “Hitting in the middle of the lineup, that’s going to happen a lot. I love those situations,” Freeman said. “Shohei stealing second was huge in that moment -- just getting 90 feet, getting into scoring position. Able to get the hit, we all got big hits tonight.” The overall effort and resilience throughout the lineup was exactly what Roberts had been searching for from his club. “I thought we fought. I thought we fought well,” Roberts said. “Tarik didn't have his best stuff ... but he didn't relent. And it was just good to see our offense really bear down -- even giving up the lead -- to come back and create a run-scoring opportunity. ... I just saw that urgency tonight, which we got to build on from here on out.” Even with Monday's win and the Dodgers still holding onto first place in the NL West by 7 1/2 games, Roberts made it clear that the time for coasting through a midseason slump has passed. “I think that we're past letting them play out of it,” Roberts said. “We're in a playoff race, trying to win the division, No. 1. No. 2, capture one of the first two playoff spots. And this is go time. So I'm going to manage accordingly. ... Everyone understands it's about winning. So it's not about feelings. I love and like everybody, but we've got to do what's best for the Dodgers for 2026.”

Tanner Scott protected the lead in the eighth with a slick 1-4-3 double play, before Edwin Díaz came on in the ninth and retired the Royals in order to lock down the save. “He was electric, and that's what we're looking for,” Muncy said of Díaz's closing effort. “We're going to expect a lot more of that in the next couple months.” For a veteran clubhouse, Monday’s battle was less about panicking and more about executing when it mattered most. “We got an older group, so I don't think we need sparks,” Freeman noted. “We know what we have to do to win games. ... There’s going to be no panic out of this clubhouse. Tonight was just a good baseball game that we played, so we’re going to carry that over tomorrow.”
